flashcards.q: What is the autoregressive factorization of a sequence's probability?
flashcards.a: p(x_1..x_n) = product over t of p(x_t | x_<t) -- each token's probability conditions only on the tokens before it.

Training technique where the model conditions each position's prediction on the TRUE ground-truth prefix from the dataset, not on the model's own previous predictions -- lets all positions' loss be computed in one parallel forward pass.

flashcards.q: Why does teacher forcing enable parallel training while RNNs could not train in parallel?
flashcards.a: Teacher forcing means no position's loss depends on another position's model output (only on the true prefix), so a causally-masked Transformer computes all positions in one batched pass. RNNs' hidden state at t is a function of the hidden state at t-1, forcing sequential computation.
The mismatch between training (conditioned on true prefixes via teacher forcing) and inference (conditioned on the model's own generated prefix, which may contain errors the model never trained on).

flashcards.q: What is the diagnostic signature that a long-generation quality problem is exposure bias specifically?
flashcards.a: Good held-out teacher-forced perplexity paired with degrading quality in free-running (autoregressive) generation as length grows -- that dissociation is the tell; if teacher-forced perplexity is also bad, look elsewhere first.

flashcards.q: What is scheduled sampling and why is it rarely used at LLM pretraining scale?
flashcards.a: Bengio et al. 2015: occasionally feed the model its own sampled prediction during training instead of the ground-truth token, annealed up over training. It directly targets exposure bias but reintroduces a sequential dependency, breaking the parallelism teacher forcing buys -- too costly at trillion-token scale.

flashcards.q: Why does RLHF/DPO/GRPO post-training partially close the exposure-bias gap that pretraining cannot?
flashcards.a: These methods score the model on sequences it actually generated autoregressively (real rollouts), not on teacher-forced likelihood -- the training distribution finally matches the deployment distribution.

flashcards.q: Why does chain-of-thought reasoning make exposure bias especially costly?
flashcards.a: Reasoning chains are long, so one early wrong intermediate step compounds into a wrong final answer -- the classic exposure-bias failure shape -- which is why RL-with-verifiable-rewards (GRPO/RLVR) trains directly against full rollouts rather than teacher-forced likelihood.

flashcards.q: Is multi-token prediction (DeepSeek-V3, Meta 2024) a fix for exposure bias?
flashcards.a: No -- it's still fully teacher-forced (all future-token targets are true tokens, not self-generated); it's a denser pretraining signal / implicit-lookahead technique, not a fix for the train/inference conditioning mismatch.

flashcards.q: Does the KV cache fix exposure bias?
flashcards.a: No -- KV caching is a speed optimization for the same sequential generation loop (avoids recomputing K/V for already-generated positions). It doesn't change what conditions the next token, so it's unrelated to exposure bias.
